newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Croatia's Tudjman says refugees can soon return.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Tudjman says refugees can soon return.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman said on Monday that local elections held earlier this month were a major step towards permitting wartime refugees to return to their homes.

Tudjman, speaking to reporters after meeting Hungarian President Arpad Goncz in Budapest, said the elections paved the way to re-establishing Croatian control over Eastern Slavonia, which is now under U.N. mandate, and that minorities including ethnic Hungarians would be safe to return.
"With the establishment of the legal system of the Croatian state it will become possible for all the people who had to leave those territories to go back," Tudjman said.
Some 80,000 war refugees are expected to move back to their homes in Eastern Slavonia after reintegration when the U.N. mandate expires in July.
Specifically addressing the issue of Croatia's Hungarian minority, Tudjman said Hungarians could return even to those villages or settlements where ethnic Serbs won a majority in the elections.

"With the introduction of the Croatian administration, those Hungarians who fled these territories will have full rights of citizenship," Tudjman said, according to a translation of his remarks into Hungarian.
According to unofficial results, former rebel Serbs won 11 of 28 municipalities in Eastern Slavonia while Croatian parties won the key city of Vukovar.

Tudjman, the 74-year-old nationalist leader who led Croatia to independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, has been battling cancer but appeared in good health in his appearance with Goncz, and stood to talk to reporters for more than 20 minutes.
